reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a flash-loan method claiming unusually rapid returns, including over 7 BNB from 0.5 BNB and approximately 200–300% profit. It directs viewers to connect MetaMask, deploy the contract, send BNB to its address, and confirm fee-bearing transactions. The educational and no-guarantee disclaimers do not change the described promotional mechanism, while the separate Ethereum giveaway is presented as subscriber engagement rather than part of that mechanism.

we need to ensure that our MetaMask wallet is connected to Remix.
the loan amount is basically the specified amount that you choose to borrow
it will initiate a flash loan
add liquidity

opening.argument: The accompanying disclosure materially qualifies the presentation: it says the content is “NOT to be considered as financial advice” and is “FOR EDUCATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY.” It also warns that cryptocurrency is “HIGHLY volatile and a very high-risk investment,” states that trading poses “considerable risk of loss,” and says the speaker “does not guarantee any particular outcome.” Those are direct risk warnings and an explicit rejection of guaranteed results. A careful reading therefore supports treating the content as qualified educational material rather than an unqualified promise of safe or certain returns.

citations.quote: This content is NOT to be considered as financial advice, legal advice or taxation advice of any kind.
FOR EDUCATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY
Cryptocurrency is HIGHLY volatile and a very high-risk investment.
The speaker does not guarantee any particular outcome.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing account emphasizes profit language but does not explain why the unusually prominent warnings should be disregarded. The disclosure expressly identifies the activity as high risk, warns of possible loss, rejects financial-advice status, and denies any guaranteed outcome. That context materially changes how statements about possible returns should be understood: they are qualified claims in an explicitly non-guaranteed educational presentation.

citations.quote: Trading cryptocurrencies poses considerable risk of loss.
The speaker does not guarantee any particular outcome.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Warnings do not erase the concrete profit pitch or the transaction workflow. The presentation says the method can produce “200 to 300% profit,” reports earning “20, even 30 BNB,” and instructs viewers to fund the contract with BNB. A disclaimer cannot make an operational inducement non-promotional merely by saying outcomes are not guaranteed.

citations.quote: you will earn approximately. 200 to 300% profit
I have earned sometimes 20, even 30 BNB using this method.
I'm going to select 0.5 BNB.

opening.argument: The primary format is a technical walkthrough. The host says he is “explaining the process behind a flash loan” and demonstrates how to implement a smart contract on Binance Smart Chain. The steps concern opening a Solidity file, copying code, compiling it, and selecting the appropriate compiler version. That is programming and operational instruction, supported by the visible Remix coding interface, rather than a general solicitation detached from a demonstrable technical process. The presenter also describes the subject as a method he is showing, which is consistent with a tutorial or demonstration format.

citations.quote: we will be explaining the process behind a flash loan.
how you can implement your very own flash loan smart contract
we paste and as we can see this pastes. All 61 lines of code of our flash loan contract into Remix.
we will need to select the compiler version 0.5

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling something a tutorial does not by itself establish deceptive promotion. The record is dominated by concrete software and blockchain instructions: create a Solidity file, paste the contract, compile it, and deploy it. Those are ordinary technical demonstration steps, and the supplied material does not independently establish that the code or reported outcome was fabricated. The educational framing is therefore a reasonable interpretation of the format.

citations.quote: this pastes. All 61 lines of code of our flash loan contract into Remix.
this is an interface which will allow us to deploy and run smart contract transactions
FOR EDUCATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The technical format does not neutralize the financial solicitation. The walkthrough goes beyond explaining code: it directs viewers to connect MetaMask, deploy the contract, send BNB to it, and activate the operation. It then presents a claimed return of 6.7 BNB from 0.4 BNB. Those instructions and outcome claims make the tutorial actionable as a profit scheme, regardless of its coding content.

the amount of liquidity to fund our contract with
from a 0.4 BNB investment, I earned back 6.7 BNB

opening.argument: The material can also be read as a software-and-service workflow around publicly named tools: MetaMask, Remix, Binance Smart Chain, and PancakeSwap. The description provides access points for those tools and explicitly limits the contract to Binance Smart Chain. Importantly, the supplied instructions do not ask viewers for passwords, recovery phrases, or credentials, and they do not describe a referral downline or membership fee. They instead describe deploying and interacting with a smart contract, while separately warning that cryptocurrency is volatile and risky. The evidence therefore does not establish the hallmark mechanisms of credential theft, guaranteed recruitment income, or a compulsory fee for access.

citations.quote: Easy to perform and no download required
This contract has been designed for Binance Smart Chain application only
we need to ensure that our MetaMask wallet is connected to Remix.
Cryptocurrency is HIGHLY volatile and a very high-risk investment.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing account treats ordinary blockchain interactions as proof of a scam mechanism, but connecting a wallet and deploying a contract are also normal operations in a smart-contract tutorial. The supplied record does not show a request for passwords, recovery phrases, or recruitment payments. It describes a network-specific contract and warns users to assess risk, so the evidence supports a technical service workflow at least as readily as the alleged mechanism.

citations.quote: This contract has been designed for Binance Smart Chain application only
Please do your own research before investing into cryptocurrency

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of credential theft or recruitment does not resolve the central issue. The method still tells viewers to send BNB to a contract and confirm fee-bearing transactions, then links that funding step to purported rapid profit. Ordinary tooling can be used in a deceptive investment pitch; the presence of MetaMask and Remix does not establish that the promised return or contract outcome is reliable.
